name: DWO WrestleKade X

date.source: The card's own repeated header: "Sunday, October 31, 2004, 8:00 p.m., LIVE! From the Carrier Dome, Syracuse, New York"; posted to the newsgroup in six parts on 13 October 2004, ahead of its own billed air date.

venue: the Carrier Dome, Syracuse, New York

appearances.note: Chose, then turned on, her own hand-picked challenger Iris Galiver in the Women's title match.
Interfered on Phoenix's behalf against Iris Galiver in the Women's title match, hours before her own Deadly Draw entry.
Ran in on the Women's title match under a mask, accidentally spearing the referee.
Returned to hit defending champion Joshua Barnes with an Eagle Claw DDT and a superkick in the Five Pillars match, avenging the career-ending loss Barnes had handed him.
Special guest referee for the Five Pillars match.
Interfered against Will Geddings and Czon Yozon on Kyle Kamikaze's behalf in the Five Pillars match.
Accompanied Kyle Kamikaze to the ring and distracted Joshua Barnes by holding his tights in the Five Pillars match.
Attacked Rick Styles backstage before the Special Challenge Match, in what was revealed after the Deadly Draw to be a staged setup with Styles.
Billed opponent for Rick Styles's Special Challenge Match; did not appear, and was replaced by Steve Douglas.
Returned from a presumed death to run in on Mike Bilodeau's behalf against Liam Rogan, ultimately delivering the finish.
Interfered on Justin Slayne's behalf in the Deadly Draw, including a baseball bat shot to Jamie Underwood.
Pulled J'ster out of the ring mid-match to save Brody Thunder in the Main Event.
Removed KC Hagen, who had distracted J'ster, on his Triad partner's behalf during the Main Event.

matches.title: dwo-1996-national
matches.note: A “Scientific Wrestling Only” stipulation broken by both men — Merc with a steel chair, Keenan with a piledriver and a chair shot of his own — before Merc pinned Keenan following three chair shots to the head. Merc's Deadly Wrestling Organization debut, after four years away from the promotion; Keenan's debut in the fed.

matches.title: dwo-1996-tag-team
matches.note: A ladder match, teaming Johnny Sledge with “Rodeo” Nevada Harris for the first time against The Riverhawks (Tommy Gibson and Mitch Hanson). Sledge did almost all of the work — catching a pair of brass knuckles Hanson dropped and using them himself — before climbing the ladder alone to pull down the belts; Harris applauded rather than helped.

matches.title: dwo-1996-womens
matches.note: Tiffany, wrestling under the ring name Phoenix, defeated Iris Galiver — “Sensuous” Samantha Bevins's own hand-picked opponent — for the vacant title after Bevins turned on Galiver mid-match with the help of a debuting “Poison Bliss” Myra Benedict, both women raising Phoenix's hand. A masked Kyle Kamikaze, wrestling as “Kinjo,” ran in on Galiver's behalf and speared the referee by mistake.

The World League Wrestling promotion's own closing title match, run on the Deadly Wrestling Organization's card by arrangement between the two promotions: a Five Pillars match, each of four elimination methods (pinfall, submission, table, stretcher) usable only once. Moved up the card after Justin Slayne's backstage attack on Rick Styles. Kyle Kamikaze won the WLW World Heavyweight Championship from defending champion Joshua Barnes with a sunset flip, after the returning “Flygod” Will Geddings (a former two-time WLW Champion) hit Barnes with an Eagle Claw DDT and a superkick, with further interference from J'ster and from Tiffany, who accompanied Kamikaze to the ring. Czon Yozon served as special guest referee.

Billed as "Top Dog" Rick Styles's retirement match against Nick Demola; Demola never appeared, and Justin Slayne attacked Styles backstage beforehand, prompting a promoter's ruling that let Styles recuperate while other matches were reordered around it. Steve Douglas stepped in as a late replacement and pinned Styles with a set of brass knuckles of his own after Styles's own knuckle shot was blocked, becoming, in the announcer's own billing, "the new Top Dog."

DWO President Mike Bilodeau's grudge match against Liam Rogan, contested through the ring, the floor and the stage. A returning "Macarena" Matt Booth — presumed dead by the broadcast team — ran in on Bilodeau's behalf, ultimately powerbombing Rogan off the entrance stage to the concrete floor for the pin.

matches.title: dwo-1996-world-heavyweight
matches.stipulation: The Deadly Draw Three, a 20-entrant, one-woman elimination match for the vacant DWO World Heavyweight Championship: four wrestlers start, two more enter every five minutes until all twenty have entered, and eliminations count only by pinfall or submission.
matches.note: "Poison Bliss" Myra Benedict eliminated six men herself before falling. "The Top Dog" Rick Styles, revealed to have been working with Justin Slayne all along despite Slayne's earlier attack on him, interfered repeatedly on Slayne's behalf, including a baseball bat shot to Jamie Underwood's head, but Underwood survived to the final two and pinned Slayne with a moonsault to become the new DWO World Heavyweight Champion. Justin Slayne and Rick Styles closed the broadcast holding the title belt aloft, having stolen it from Underwood after the bell.

matches.stipulation: Two out of three falls, the two falls to be scored consecutively
matches.note: J'ster stabbed Brody Thunder's leg with a switchblade in the early going and worked it for the rest of the match, taking the first fall off a distraction by KC Hagen (removed by J'ster's own Triad partner Joshua Barnes) and finishing Thunder with a sharpshooter; Thunder refused to submit and passed out from blood loss, ending the match without a tap. DWO World Champion Jamie Underwood pulled J'ster out of the ring mid-match to save Thunder from a following count.

name: DWO Deadly Draw 2

date.source: Billed throughout the promotion's own build-up broadcasts (April 1999) for "MAY 16th, LIVE in San Antonio Texas"; the results were posted to the newsgroup in eight parts between 20 and 24 May 1999.

venue: the Alamo Dome, San Antonio, Texas

appearances.note: Special referee for Mike Bilodeau's own First Blood match; attacks Bilodeau with the DWO title belt after the decision.
Seizes the DWO presidency on air, books a fake Robski/Brody Thunder match as a stunt, and has DWO Owner Mike Bilodeau arrested by the card's end.
Shot on a videotape shown mid-card in a confrontation with Mike Bilodeau; a masked impostor wearing his gear interferes in the Deadly Rumble.
Accompanies Sick Rick to the ring for the Deadly Rumble and is lifted onto his shoulders after the win.
Teams with Jawaad Mahmood as the Mahmood Brothers in an Ultimate Barb Wire match against Apollo and Moo Kame, ambushed by interference before the bell.
Teams with Razi Mahmood as the Mahmood Brothers in an Ultimate Barb Wire match against Apollo and Moo Kame, ambushed by interference before the bell.
Teams with Al Robertson in the Double Lethal Round Robin match, ultimately eliminated when Mike Bilodeau (wrestling as Nick Leshenn's mystery partner) DDTs him.
Forced into a two-ring Lethal Scaffold match against his own Suicidal Stallions partner Mad Bronco, dropkicked off the scaffold and eliminated.

matches.stipulation: Steel Cage Showdown: both members of the losing team must leave the cage
matches.note: A crossover match previewed weeks earlier on MCW's own Gold Rush broadcast. Cris Rio is press-slammed through the cage door and walks out, leaving Nicklaus Kain alone; Mr. Fantastic finishes Kain with the Thrill Ride, then Gorilla turns on his own partner afterward.

matches.stipulation: Lethal First Blood match, special referee Professor Payne
matches.note: DWO Owner Mike Bilodeau's own open-challenge match. Payne declares Bilodeau the winner by first blood after a belt shot busts Erottika open, then attacks Bilodeau with the belt anyway; Apollo runs in and knocks Payne out.

matches.title: dwo-1996-world-heavyweight
matches.stipulation: The Deadly Rumble, a twenty-entrant battle royal for the vacant DWO World Heavyweight Championship; entrants join every five minutes, eliminated by pinfall, submission or over the top rope with both feet on the floor.

eliminations.note: Clotheslined over the top rope from behind.
Pinned with a cement brick shot.
Bulldogged into a school bus radiator and pinned.
Tapped out to his own hold, the Extreme End, used against him.
Rolled up from behind and pinned.
Chokeslammed, then pinned with a Leshenn Driver.
Piledriven onto a steel chair, set up by a Mike Bilodeau chair shot to Sick Rick.
Pinned after Mike Bilodeau's own chair shot missed Sick Rick and hit Apollo instead, and Sick Rick used a set of brass knuckles.

matches.note: Four further entrants (Moo Kame, Mr. Cody Young, "Hot Stuff" Scott Richards and Mr. Fantastic) also competed in the held record's broadcast; their eliminations are not separately recorded here. The ring collapses mid-match under a 300-foot fall from the rafters and the bout finishes in the parking lot.

date.source: The card's own header, "Sunday, November 28, 1999, TOKYO, JAPAN," matching the date the results were posted to the newsgroup.

appearances.note: Special guest referee for the Dysfunction Classic; helps ambush and attack Matt Booth after the bell, and is arrested for it.
Hands Sick Rick a set of brass knuckles during his losing DWO World Title defense.
Billed and retains the DWO World Tag Team Championship against the Natural Born Killers, a match not otherwise structured in the held record's records.
Manages the Perfectly Perfect Duo; her own attempted interference with a title belt backfires before the Duo retains anyway.
Manages "Top Dog" Rick Styles in the promotion's own last match, interfering with a steel chair.
Walks out of his own Hall of Fame induction match against Magnus Colby rather than compete after Matt Booth's on-air attack; fired from the promotion for it.
Revealed to have spent the broadcast's early hours locked in his own office by an impostor twin; restored to the show and has Liam Rogan's crew arrested.
Arrested alongside Liam Rogan for the on-air attack on Matt Booth before her own billed Women's Challenge match against Sandy Fox could take place.
Billed for a Women's Challenge match against Kieran Erottika that never takes place after her husband Matt Booth's on-air attack and Erottika's own arrest.
Inducted into the DWO Hall of Fame in absentia alongside his brother Jawaad.
Inducted into the DWO Hall of Fame in absentia alongside his brother Razi.
Inducted into the DWO Hall of Fame in absentia as the promotion's own co-founder.

matches.stipulation: "I Quit" match, special guest referee Liam Rogan
matches.note: Billed "The Dysfunction Classic." Rogan and a hidden Jay Ralston ambush Sandy Fox and handcuff Matt Booth to the ropes; Dark Vanity holds Booth's legs so Rogan can assault him, and Booth screams "I quit" during the attack. Reported dead of blood loss afterward; revealed alive in the broadcast's closing segment, the whole attack a trap sprung on Rogan's own crew.

matches.stipulation: Hall of Fame Match, Last Man Standing
matches.note: Apollo pulls a rigged cable that buries Alex Extreme under a pile of bricks; the referee's ten count runs out with Extreme still buried.

Both men trade finishers, including a Martinez legdrop off the top of the cage through the Spanish announce table. Neither man escapes before both are counted out cold; DWO Owner Mike Bilodeau rules the match a double advancement into the Final Fight tournament's next round.

matches.title: dwo-1996-world-heavyweight
matches.stipulation: DWO World Heavyweight Championship, no disqualification, falls count anywhere
matches.note: Sick Rick's mystery challenger is revealed as Jeff "Madfox" Matthews. The brawl runs through the parking garage and onto a tour bus before Matthews finishes Sick Rick with a top-rope powerbomb to become the promotion's own last World Champion.

matches.stipulation: Eight-man Thunderdome elimination match, the Final Fight tournament's own last round: two four-man teams locked in a Hell in a Cell, eliminated by being handcuffed to the cage.

eliminations.note: Leshenn Driver into the cage bars, then handcuffed.
Handcuffed to the cage after a Firebomb Chokeslam.
Handcuffed to the cage after a full nelson suplex.

matches.note: Three further competitors (the Golden Haired Fox, Havoc and Jack Rogers) also entered the held record's broadcast; their eliminations are not separately recorded here. In the final two, Alex Martinez handcuffs himself to the roof of the cage rather than fall after blocking a Leshenn Driver, giving Nick Leshenn the win by default, then firebomb-chokeslams Leshenn through the cage roof anyway.

matches.stipulation: Hall of Fame Match, two out of three falls; the promotion's own last match
matches.note: A ten-bell salute opens the bout. After a disputed shared-pinfall first decision voids a fired referee's call, Rick Styles and Professor Payne split the first two falls before Payne wins the third with an Outsider's Edge; the broadcast team declares the Deadly Wrestling Organization closed.
